summary: Ray and a companion agree on Thai food and go to Bangkok House on Paraclete, run by Ng Uk-Thong. The note describes the rats' habits: they sleep late, trade during the afternoon, and queue for the broadcast array that Commander Sorensen allows only in the evening. At the nearly empty restaurant, Uk-Thong's wife Maria Concita runs the counter alone and shouts abuse at the kitchen staff. The passage mixes comic description with commentary on the rats' lives and the Thai approach to recycling.
one_line: Ray and a companion visit Bangkok House on Paraclete, where the rats' late-night schedule and Maria Concita's loud management style set the scene.
key_facts: Ray has never been able to fathom why Thai trash is always a rat favorite.
Ng Uk-Thong is the Thai franchisee on Paraclete.
Ng Uk-Thong steadfastly refuses to strike a food-for-labor deal with the system vets.
The note says Uk-Thong sees no reason to make compromises with mere carbon-form emissaries.
The chefs at Uk-Thong's Bangkok House used a good food processor, so they generated very little raw waste.
Commander Sorensen does not let the rats use the broadcast array until late in the evening.
The rats now rise late and plot their fiscal strategies in the hours between noon and six.
The rats queue outside the Network Control hub just off the auxiliary communications bridge.
Bangkok House is nearly deserted when Ray and his companion arrive.
Maria Concita, Ng Uk-Thong's dowdy Brazilian wife, mans the service counter alone from a stool behind the cash register.
Maria Concita wears a floral print sarong and displays a length of cleavage the note says could be detected by satellite reconnaissance.
Maria Concita is known for a hostile and howling management style aimed at the kitchen's chaos.
Maria Concita threatens that Gucho will cut throats with a box knife if the kitchen keeps dropping dishes.
Maria Concita tells a customer the chicken is fresh from the flash freeze unit this morning.
